headline: 16 million people are online. A fad, say the sceptics
text: At the end of 1995 about 16 million people in the world used the internet, less than half a percent of mankind. Not everybody believes it will matter. 'The Internet? Bah!' wrote the astronomer Clifford Stoll in Newsweek last February: no online database would replace the daily newspaper, and people would not shop over a computer. Robert Metcalfe, who invented the Ethernet network cable, predicts that the internet will collapse this year under its own growth, and has promised to eat his words if it does not.
source: https://www.stackscale.com/blog/internet-evolution-statistics/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.allaboutmarketresearch.com/internet.htm (search result read 2026-10-04) (figures of Internet World Stats); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clifford_Stoll (read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Metcalfe (read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: Robert Metcalfe (photograph from 2004)

headline: Gil Amelio replaces Spindler; Apple's survival in question
text: On 2 February Apple named Gil Amelio, head of National Semiconductor, as chief executive, replacing Michael Spindler. Apple could not build enough of its popular models and too many of the others, its finance chief left in 1995 after urging a sale of the company, and merger talks with IBM, Sun and Philips came to nothing. Fortune wrote this month that the company that invented the personal computer will likely disappear.
imageCaption: Gil Amelio, Apple's new chief executive, in a television interview, 1996

headline: Microsoft gives its browser away; Netscape's shares fall
text: Netscape began shipping Navigator 2.0 on 5 February, with more than a thousand small Java programs already written for it. But its shares, which peaked in early December, have fallen hard. On 7 December Bill Gates said Microsoft would embrace the internet and give its own browser, Internet Explorer, away, 'free forever', while Netscape asks companies and most users to pay for Navigator. And six months after the public offering, employees who had agreed not to sell 22.8 million shares are now free to sell them.
source: https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease82.html (press release of 5 February 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=19970311&slug=2528165 (Seattle Times on Gates's speech of 7 December 1995, read 2026-10-14); https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19960316/2319160/netscape-execs-sold-shares-as-stock-fell (Seattle Times, 16 March 1996, on the lock-up of 22.8 million shares and the fall since December, read 2026-10-14)
imageCaption: A floppy disk with Microsoft Internet Explorer 2.0 for Windows 95 (Swiss-German edition); its label says it may be copied and passed on freely

headline: Coca-Cola worth 93 billion dollars after a 46% year
text: Coca-Cola's shares rose 44% in 1995, ahead of the S&P 500, for a total return of 46%. Its market value reached nearly 93 billion dollars, up 27 billion in a year. Net income rose 17% to almost 3 billion dollars. The company has bought back large amounts of its own shares, which it says lifted earnings per share growth to 18% a year.
imageCaption: Coca-Cola headquarters, Atlanta

headline: McDonald's opens a restaurant every few hours
text: McDonald's opened 1,130 restaurants in the United States alone in 1995 and is expanding even faster abroad, approaching 20,000 restaurants in total. Franchisees complain that new restaurants are taking sales from existing ones, and sales at US restaurants open more than a year are flat.
imageCaption: McDonald's golden arches sign

headline: Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy to merge as Novartis
text: On 7 March Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy, Basel's old rivals, announced that they will merge into a new company called Novartis, the largest corporate merger ever; the two had combined sales of nearly $30 billion last year. Ciba-Geigy's chairman Alex Krauer is to be chairman and Sandoz's pharma chief Daniel Vasella chief executive. Sandoz's bearer share jumped 23% in March, Ciba-Geigy's 38%.
source: https://live.novartis.com/en/article/49 (read 2026-10-03); https://pmlive.com/pharma_news/this_month_in_1996_ciba-geigy_and_sandoz_merge_553502 (read 2026-10-03); search excerpt of https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/cen-v074n011.p007 (combined sales, read 2026-10-03); NZZ prices in data/manual/raw/nzz-notes-1995-1998.md (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Marc Moret of Sandoz (left), Daniel Vasella, chief executive designate of Novartis, and Alex Krauer of Ciba-Geigy announce the merger, Basel, March 1996

headline: Liggett breaks ranks and settles
text: In March the small cigarette maker Liggett, with about 2% of the US market, agreed to settle smoking-and-health lawsuits, the first company to do so. Philip Morris and the other big makers say they will not settle and will fight every case. At the end of 1995 there were 125 smoking-and-health cases pending against Philip Morris, 88 of them filed in Florida since April 1995, and several states are suing to recover Medicaid costs. Geoffrey Bible is chairman and chief executive.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764180/0000950146-96-000483.txt (Philip Morris 10-K for 1995, filed March 1996, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liggett_Group (read 2026-10-03); month change from data/out/mo.json
imageCaption: Bennett LeBow, owner of Liggett ;;

headline: Exxon's profit rises 27 percent
text: Exxon's accounts for 1995 show net income of 6.47 billion dollars, up from 5.10 billion in 1994, and a higher dividend. Chemicals earned twice as much as in 1994.
source: Exxon Form 10-K405 for 1997, selected financial data (1993-1997, post-split basis), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/0000930661-98-000526.txt (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Lee Raymond, Exxon's chairman and chief executive

headline: Cisco buys StrataCom for about $4 billion
text: Cisco agreed on April 22 to acquire StrataCom, a maker of high-speed switches used by telephone carriers, in exchange for Cisco shares. Each StrataCom share is to be exchanged for about one Cisco share, putting the deal at around $4 billion, one of the largest in the industry. Chambers said Cisco will be the only vendor to offer connections across public and private networks.
imageCaption: StrataCom's switching systems, c. 1996
imageCredit: Cisco Systems (Center for Cisco Heritage archive, Computer History Museum)

headline: Netscape beats forecasts as the Nasdaq sets records
text: Netscape reported on 23 April revenue of $55 million for the first quarter, 35% more than in the last quarter of 1995, and a profit of $4.7 million, more than Wall Street expected. It is shipping Navigator 2.0 and has unveiled SuiteSpot, a set of server programs for companies' internal networks, or 'intranets'. Its shares rose for two days in a market that loves technology: on 24 April the Nasdaq index closed at a record for the fifth day running, on the busiest day in Wall Street's history. On 29 April Netscape introduced Navigator 3.0.
source: https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease127.html (press release of 23 April 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://www.spokesman.com/stories/1996/apr/25/dow-tumbles-on-wall-streets-busiest-day/ (Spokesman-Review, 25 April 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease129.html (press release of 29 April 1996, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Bankgesellschaft rejects a merger with CS Holding
text: On the night of 11 April the Bankgesellschaft's board unanimously rejected a merger proposal from CS Holding, whose chairman Rainer Gut had telephoned Nikolaus Senn with the offer. The combined bank would have earned slightly more than 3 billion francs a year and, with a balance sheet of about $419 billion, would have ranked second in the world. A merger could have cost up to 10,000 jobs in Switzerland.
imageCaption: The Bankgesellschaft's headquarters on the Bahnhofstrasse, Zurich

headline: Technology shares slump; Microsoft builds its browser into Windows
text: Technology shares fell sharply in July: by 25 July the Nasdaq index was 15% below its record of 5 June. Netscape reported on 18 July revenue of $75 million for the second quarter, 34% more than in the first, but its profit fell to $906,000 after $6.1 million of costs for three acquisitions. On 22 July the New York Times reported that Microsoft will build its own web browser into a new version of Windows 95 and distribute it later this summer.
source: https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease191.html (press release of 18 July 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://www.spokesman.com/stories/1996/jul/23/stocks-slide-again-investor-sentiment-worsens/ (Spokesman-Review, 23 July 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://www.spokesman.com/stories/1996/jul/26/nasdaq-system-takes-troubles-in-stride-blunders/ (Spokesman-Review, 26 July 1996, read 2026-10-14)

headline: Enron to buy Oregon utility Portland General
text: Enron has agreed to buy Portland General Corporation, an Oregon electric utility, for about 51 million new Enron shares worth about $2.1 billion, plus about $1.1 billion of Portland General's debt. Enron calls the combination the nation's largest integrated natural gas and electricity company, with 5,900 megawatts of generating capacity and 37,000 miles of pipeline.
imageCaption: Kenneth Lay, Enron's chairman and chief executive, in his office at the company's Houston headquarters, February 1996
imageCredit: Paul S. Howell | Hulton Archive | Getty Images

headline: The summer of the Macarena, and a phone that sends e-mail
text: The Macarena, a Spanish song with a dance that everyone can do, reached number one in the American charts in August and its dance has become a craze. On 15 August Nokia put on sale the 9000 Communicator, a mobile phone that opens like a small laptop with a keyboard and can send faxes and e-mail; in Britain it costs about 1,000 pounds.
imageCaption: The Nokia 9000 Communicator, opened like a small laptop

headline: Wal-Mart opens in China
text: In August Wal-Mart opened a Supercenter and a Sam's Club in Shenzhen, China; about 80,000 people came on the first day. Wal-Mart already trades in Mexico and Canada and is looking for growth abroad as growth at home slows.
imageCaption: Entrance of a Wal-Mart store in Shenzhen, China, 2005
imageCredit: No machine-readable author provided. Chancelle assumed (based on copyright claims).

headline: Navigator 3.0 is downloaded 2.5 million times in two weeks
text: The browser war is on. Microsoft released Internet Explorer 3.0 in August, and Netscape followed with Navigator 3.0 on 19 August; Netscape has also complained to the Justice Department that Microsoft breaks the law. On 4 September Netscape said that users had downloaded more than 2.5 million copies of Navigator 3.0 in its first two weeks, and that Navigator, with more than 40 million users, remains the most popular internet program in the world. Its web site now gets more than 100 million hits a day.
source: https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease229.html (press release of 4 September 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://web.archive.org/web/1998/http://home.netscape.com/newsref/pr/newsrelease238.html (press release of 11 September 1996, read 2026-10-14); https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=19970311&slug=2528165 (Seattle Times, on the August 1996 releases and the complaint, read 2026-10-14)
imageCaption: Netscape Navigator 3 Gold

headline: Wall Street rediscovers IBM
text: IBM shares jumped more than 17 dollars in a few days to their highest in nine years, as analysts raised their targets: Merrill Lynch sees 195 dollars, Argus 175. 'It's really not a recovery, it's a discovery of IBM,' one analyst said. On 26 November the board approved buying back up to 3.5 billion dollars of stock.
imageCaption: Louis Gerstner at the National Education Summit, 1996

headline: Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy become Novartis
text: The merger of Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy, announced on 7 March as the largest corporate merger ever, is being completed: Sandoz shares, last traded on 29 November, are exchanged for shares of the new Novartis. Ciba-Geigy's chairman Alex Krauer is chairman and Sandoz's Daniel Vasella chief executive.
imageCaption: The Ciba logo with the Sandoz building behind it, Basel

headline: Clinton re-elected; Perot takes 8%
text: Bill Clinton won a second term on 5 November with 379 electoral votes and 49.2% of the vote against Bob Dole's 40.7%; Ross Perot, running again as an independent, took 8.4%. The economy is growing, inflation is low and the stock market has doubled since Clinton took office, which left Dole little to run on.
imageCaption: Supporters at a Clinton-Gore campaign rally in Las Cruces, New Mexico, 1 November 1996

headline: Sandoz leaves the market
text: Merged with Ciba-Geigy into Novartis. The shares are no longer traded.
imageCaption: The Ciba logo with the Sandoz building behind it, Basel

headline: Apple buys NeXT, and Jobs is back
text: On 20 December Apple announced it will buy NeXT, Steve Jobs's company, for 429 million dollars and 1.5 million Apple shares. NeXT's operating system will become the basis of the next Mac system, which Apple failed to build itself, and the deal brings Jobs back into Apple's management.
imageCaption: Steve Jobs presenting in front of the NeXT logo, 1990s

headline: Greenspan asks about 'irrational exuberance'; shares end 1996 up 20 percent
text: On 5 December Fed chairman Alan Greenspan asked in a speech how one can know 'when irrational exuberance has unduly escalated asset values'. Tokyo, open at the time, fell 3% and markets around the world followed. Still, the S&P 500 ended 1996 up 20% at 740.74, and the Dow, which passed 6,000 on 14 October, up 26%.
imageCaption: President Bill Clinton walks with Alan Greenspan at the White House after nominating him for a third term as Fed chairman, 22 February 1996
imageCredit: Jim Colburn / AFP via Getty Images (credit from the Getty record of the picture, GettyImages-51975024)
